_doc: Round 17 — the custom class. Everything here is the TUNING a point-buy character needs and nothing here is a copy of anything. The spell tier list itself is NOT in this file: js/classbuild.js derives it at load from data/classes.json and data/skills.json, because those two are already the source of truth for all 30 preset classes and a committed copy of them would drift the first time somebody adds a skill. See CLASSES.md, 'Where the tier list comes from'.
_customDoc: The synthetic class a custom build is injected as. `id` is what ends up in the save's `classId`, which is why it must never collide with one of the 30 real ones.

custom.name: Freelance
custom.hook: Nothing came with this one. Every spell on the bar was chosen.

_tierDoc: The six rungs, mirroring data/skills.json's `unlockAt`. A spell's TIER is the earliest rung any of the 30 classes hands it out on; a pick may only take a spell whose tier is at or below the rung being filled, which is the whole of the point-buy rule. The levels below are a cross-check, not a second source: js/classbuild.js asserts they match skills.json and throws if they do not, because two ladders that disagree is the bug this project keeps finding.

tiers.name: Opening
tiers.blurb: What you walk out of the gate holding.

tiers.name: Second
tiers.blurb: The first thing you learn from being hit.

tiers.name: Third
tiers.blurb: Where a build starts to have a shape.

tiers.name: Fourth
tiers.blurb: The answer to whatever keeps killing you.

tiers.name: Fifth
tiers.blurb: The one that costs something to cast.

tiers.name: Sixth
tiers.blurb: The last slot. Spend it on the fight you keep losing.

_loadoutDoc: Every sensible pair of hands. `main` and `off` are weaponBase keys out of the shared items.json; `offArmour` is an off-hand ARMOUR base (a shield, a focus, a quiver) rather than a second weapon. `needsPerk` names a perk-forest keystone by its KEYSTONE id — a saved perk is the node id, so js/classbuild.js looks the node up through the forest rather than hard-coding one. `element` marks the loadouts that carry a branded caster and therefore get an element picker.

loadouts.name: Blade and Board
loadouts.blurb: A longsword and something to get in the way. The build that survives its own mistakes.

loadouts.name: Hammer and Board
loadouts.blurb: Slow, heavy and very hard to walk past.

loadouts.name: Spear and Shield
loadouts.blurb: Four metres of reach behind a shield. You hit them first and they stay hit.

loadouts.name: Javelin and Buckler
loadouts.blurb: Throwable, and light enough to keep a hand free.

loadouts.name: Two Blades
loadouts.blurb: Two swords on two clocks. The off hand hits for less and never stops.

loadouts.name: Knife Pair
loadouts.blurb: Short reach, twice the speed, and everything bleeds.

loadouts.name: Rapier and Knife
loadouts.blurb: Thrust, thrust, lunge — and a knife for whatever closes.

loadouts.name: Great Blade
loadouts.blurb: A wide sweep and a slow overhead that catches everything in front of you.

loadouts.name: Great Axe
loadouts.blurb: Nothing subtle. Cleaves through the front rank into the one behind it.

loadouts.name: Halberd
loadouts.blurb: Seven metres of pierce line. Everything standing in a row is one swing.

loadouts.name: Quarterstaff
loadouts.blurb: A pole, not a wand. Fast, long and it costs nothing to carry.

loadouts.name: Bow and Quiver
loadouts.blurb: A real draw, and the further it flies the harder it lands.

loadouts.name: Crossbow and Quiver
loadouts.blurb: Slower than a bow and it does not care what you are wearing.

loadouts.name: Wand and Focus
loadouts.blurb: Thirty-four metres of branded bolt, and a focus in the other hand.

loadouts.name: Wand and Tome
loadouts.blurb: Both hands casting. Nothing to block with at all.

loadouts.name: Elemental Staff
loadouts.blurb: Swung, not aimed — and every swing is the element you chose.

loadouts.name: Sceptre and Shield
loadouts.blurb: The one that casts and still stands in the front rank.

loadouts.name: Two Two-Handers
loadouts.blurb: A greatsword in each hand. Only possible once the grip that frees a hand is taken.

_elementDoc: What a branded caster may be attuned to. These are rpg.js's own CAST_ELEMENTS keys — js/classbuild.js checks each one resolves there, so a choice can never be an element the game does not have.

elements.name: Storm
elements.blurb: Leaves the target taking more of everything.

elements.name: Arc
elements.blurb: Raw force — no status, and the hardest hitting.

_armourDoc: What each armour tier puts on you at level 1. Base keys out of items.json, equipped exactly the way a preset class's `startingArmour` is.
_openingDoc: The one choice the user asked for by name: somebody to walk with you, or a crate and some money for the people who would rather be alone. A companion is a bestiary pet id out of data/enemies.json, so it is a real body with real numbers. The crate is rolled through rpg.loot the same way every chest in the game is — `floor` is the worst rarity it can hold, which is what makes 'three magic or better' a promise rather than a hope.

companions.name: A wolf
companions.blurb: Fast, bites hard, dies to anything that looks at it twice.

companions.name: A dire hound
companions.blurb: The heavy one. Walks in first and stays there.

companions.name: A hunting cat
companions.blurb: Goes for whatever is casting and is never where the swing lands.

companions.name: A bone thrall
companions.blurb: Cheap, expendable, and there are two of them.

companions.name: An ember familiar
companions.blurb: Hangs back and burns things from twenty metres.

companions.name: A storm familiar
companions.blurb: Shocks what it hits, so everything else lands harder.

companions.name: A spirit bear
companions.blurb: Slow and enormous. Nothing gets past it quickly.

companions.name: A clockwork sentry
companions.blurb: Shoots over your shoulder and never needs feeding.

companions.name: A bound imp
companions.blurb: Casts, complains, and is much stronger than it looks.

crate.name: A Sealed Chest
crate.blurb: Three things of magic quality or better, and enough coin to buy a fourth.

_lookDoc: Which of the 30 class looks a custom character borrows its body from before the appearance editor gets to it. Nothing but a starting point — Customize on the character step replaces the whole avatar.
